# Synthetic xoshiro128** golden vectors

`xoshiro128ss-v1.json` freezes Math Adventure's `xoshiro128ss-v1` behavior. It contains synthetic state only: three seeds, sixteen consecutive unsigned outputs and post-draw states for each seed (48 transitions), nine bounded-choice scenarios, and eight malformed/all-zero seed cases. It contains no learner data.

## Provenance and independence

The original authors' [xoshiro128** C reference](https://prng.di.unimi.it/xoshiro128starstar.c), by David Blackman and Sebastiano Vigna, was retrieved on **2026-10-05**. The source identifies version **1.1** and uses state word `s[1]` in its output scrambler. Version 1.0's `s[0]` output is a different algorithm and is excluded. The authors' [PRNG overview](https://prng.di.unimi.it/) describes the generator as non-cryptographic.

The fixture was generated by [the test-only independent reference model](../../oracle/xoshiro-reference.ts), without importing or executing production RNG code. That model uses unbounded BigInt arithmetic, modulo `2^32`, BigInt XOR and quotient/remainder rotation; production uses JavaScript unsigned 32-bit bitwise operations. Its simultaneous state equations are algebraically derived from the author's ordered transition. This avoids sharing production rotation helpers, JavaScript signed-bitwise handling or the production state update implementation.

A separate hand calculation cross-checks the first low-word transition. From `[1, 2, 3, 4]`, `(2 × 5) × 2^7 × 9 = 11520` without wraparound. The XOR intermediates are `3 XOR 1 = 2` and `4 XOR 2 = 6`, giving next state `[7, 0, 1026, 12288]`. The fixture agrees with both this result and the BigInt model. These are independently calculated fixtures, not published author vectors.

## Frozen mapping and bounded choice

Each seed is exactly 32 hexadecimal digits. Characters `0..7`, `8..15`, `16..23`, `24..31` encode unsigned words `s0`, `s1`, `s2`, `s3`, each most-significant hexadecimal digit first. Both letter cases are accepted; canonical seed/state text is lowercase. All-zero state is rejected. There is no byte-endianness conversion, seed expansion or seed generation.

Bound `n` means the half-open output interval `[0, n)` for integers `1 ≤ n ≤ 2^32`. The acceptance threshold is `floor(2^32 / n) × n`. Draws at or above it are rejected and still consume a state transition. An accepted draw maps by its remainder modulo `n`. This accepted interval contains exactly `floor(2^32 / n)` representatives of each remainder, proving unbiased mapping for a uniformly distributed unsigned input; this is not a statistical proof of PRNG independence or cryptographic strength.

The default attempt cap is 128, with an explicit cap in `1..128`. Exhaustion preserves the consumed final state and draw count. The all-ones fixture at bound `2147483649` rejects three high outputs before accepting `2943360` on draw four; its cap-one counterpart exhausts after consuming the first state transition. Bound one consumes one draw even though its selected value is always zero. Power-of-two, non-power-of-two, maximum and near-maximum bounds are included.

Any change to word mapping, scrambler, rotations, state transition, draw-consumption or bounded-choice behavior needs a new RNG algorithm ID. Never regenerate this fixture merely to make changed production code pass.

## Reproduction

With the repository's pinned Node 24.21.0, its native TypeScript stripping can run the test-only model without compiling production code:

```powershell
node --input-type=module -e "import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'; import { createXoshiroGoldenFixture } from './tests/oracle/xoshiro-reference.ts'; writeFileSync('tests/fixtures/golden/xoshiro128ss-v1.json', JSON.stringify(createXoshiroGoldenFixture(), null, 2) + String.fromCharCode(10));"
corepack pnpm exec prettier --write tests/fixtures/golden/xoshiro128ss-v1.json
```

Review the resulting diff, source and manual calculation independently. Ordinary Vitest domain tests compare every frozen transition and bounded outcome with production; they can run unchanged on the existing Windows/Linux CI configuration. Hosted Phase 1B execution remains future owner-authorized PR evidence.
